purpose: Bounded CFPB route from Bilt bank-partner transition through customer fees, provider outreach, reported reimbursement, technical repair, and open individual recovery.

events.geography: United States; Bilt customers affected by a bank-partner transition
events.date_precision: CFPB newsroom account reviewed in June 2026; reimbursement milestone refers to more than 500 newly identified customers by June 4, 2026
events.denominator: Affected Bilt customers are not fully enumerated; the public account reports some customers with transition-related problems and a milestone for more than 500 newly identified customers
events.method: Official CFPB account of a collaborative consumer-remediation process and Bilt documentation; no account-level customer file is retained
events.missingness: Affected-account denominator, failed-payment date, fee amount, contact success, reimbursement receipt, account correction, credit effect, repeat failure, continued use, trust, and switching are not linked
events.exposure: Bilt's transition to a new bank partner created technical problems for some customers, including overdraft, late, and insufficient-funds fees
events.alternatives_before_action: Customers may have contacted Bilt, absorbed fees, borrowed, changed payment routes, disputed charges, or switched providers, but the public record does not identify which routes were feasible or used
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Technical failure could create fees, payment timing risk, and administrative work; the provider's outreach and reimbursement offer created a formal route without showing equal reach or immediate liquidity restoration
events.choice_or_response: Bilt proactively contacted potentially affected customers, offered reimbursement, reviewed newly identified requests, and reported technical issues as resolved; CFPB reported reimbursement for more than 500 newly identified customers by June 4, 2026
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Bilt and its bank partners control system migration, account processing, outreach, and reimbursement; customers control contact, dispute, payment substitution, and switching choices under uneven time and liquidity constraints
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Provider outreach, reimbursement review, and reported technical repair are visible; individual payment receipt, account correction, and independent verification are not
events.immediate_outcome: The route establishes a firm-level transition, customer-fee exposure, proactive remediation, and reported system repair while leaving customer recovery open
events.protected_outcome: Accurate account balances, fee-free payment processing, restored liquidity, and continued financial access could be protected by reimbursement and technical repair, but no individual protected outcome is verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Money, time, credit standing, payment reliability, trust, and provider choice may be sacrificed; the public record does not measure each customer's trade-off
events.cost_risk_transfer: A bank-partner migration can transfer technical, overdraft, late-fee, documentation, and contact costs between firm, bank, payment network, and customer; the public account does not quantify the transfer
events.later_outcome: No same-customer reimbursement receipt, account correction, credit repair, repeat failure, continued use, switching, or durable financial recovery is observed
events.meaning_and_attribution: A customer may interpret the transition as ordinary technical failure, institutional negligence, or a reason to leave; fairness, blame, trust, and attribution are not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: CFPB oversight and collaborative remediation are observed; customer complaints, collective action, political response, and later market switching are not linked
events.counterexample: Proactive outreach and reimbursement for newly identified customers may resolve many cases; the public record cannot establish that all affected customers were identified, contacted, reimbursed, or harmed equally
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official CFPB agency-reported consumer-recourse account; no customer-level denominator, payment file, independent technical audit, or later outcome is published in the retained record

events.geography: United States; Bilt consumers eligible for transition-related reimbursement
events.date_precision: CFPB page reports reimbursement status as of September 10, 2026 and CFPB closure notification on September 21, 2026
events.denominator: More than 2,000 eligible consumers; CFPB reports total reimbursement of $264,792.71
events.method: Later dated update on the same official CFPB newsroom account; aggregate remediation report, not a retained customer-level payment file
events.missingness: Individual payment receipt, timing, fee-level allocation, account correction, credit effect, repeat failure, adequacy, continued use, trust, and switching remain unlinked
events.exposure: Previously reported transition-related overdraft, late, and insufficient-funds fees for affected consumers
events.alternatives_before_action: Consumers could seek reimbursement, absorb losses, alter payment routes, or switch, but the later update does not identify individual paths
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The aggregate report indicates a completed reimbursement program for eligible consumers, while leaving the distribution timing and adequacy of each payment unobserved
events.choice_or_response: Bilt reported reimbursing all eligible consumers and the CFPB notified Bilt that it considered the matter closed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Bilt controlled reimbursement execution; CFPB controlled oversight and closure; consumers retained any account correction, dispute, or switching choices
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Aggregate reimbursement of $264,792.71 to more than 2,000 eligible consumers and CFPB case closure are reported
events.immediate_outcome: The public route now reaches aggregate redress completion and regulatory closure, not just an offer or review stage
events.protected_outcome: Reimbursement may restore some charged funds, but restoration of liquidity, credit position, payment reliability, or trust is not verified at the individual level
events.sacrificed_outcome: Any unreimbursed non-fee loss, delayed access, credit effect, administrative effort, or continued disruption remains unmeasured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The reported reimbursement shifts identified fee costs back toward the firm, but the public update does not quantify residual or non-fee costs
events.later_outcome: Aggregate reimbursement and case closure are observed; same-customer receipt, adequacy, repeat failure, continued use, switching, and durable financial recovery remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: Closure may be read as effective resolution or as an institutional endpoint that does not capture lived recovery; interpretation is not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: CFPB oversight reaches a reported closure; no linked customer-level complaint, appeal, or later market response is published
events.counterexample: All eligible consumers may have received adequate reimbursement and experienced no lasting effect; the aggregate update cannot test that counterexample at the person level
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official CFPB update with aggregate eligibility and payment totals; no independent payment audit, account-level file, or customer follow-up is published in the retained record

arrows.evidence: CFPB reports that the transition created technical issues and overdraft, late, and insufficient-funds fees for some Bilt customers
arrows.counterexample: The public account does not establish the affected denominator, individual causation, or whether every fee was ultimately valid or reversed
arrows.remaining_gap: Affected account, failure date, fee amount, payment timing, credit effect, and customer burden

arrows.evidence: Bilt proactively contacted potentially affected customers, offered reimbursement, and reviewed requests; CFPB reported reimbursement for more than 500 newly identified customers by June 4, 2026
arrows.counterexample: An outreach or reimbursement milestone is not proof of contact, issuance, receipt, or adequacy for each affected customer
arrows.remaining_gap: Affected denominator, contact success, eligibility, payment issuance, receipt, account correction, and residual loss

arrows.evidence: CFPB reported that the technical issues appeared resolved and that submitted documentation appeared to show the process was complete
arrows.counterexample: Agency-reported technical resolution does not establish independent verification, account correction, or absence of repeat failures
arrows.remaining_gap: Independent repair test, account-level correction, repeat-failure rate, and continued service reliability

arrows.to: restored liquidity, credit position, and durable customer security
arrows.evidence: The public account does not link affected customers to payment receipt, fee reversal, credit correction, repeat failure, or later financial room
arrows.counterexample: A customer may recover through another account or absorb a small fee without a measurable later crisis; neither outcome is observed
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-customer receipt, account/credit correction, adequacy, repeat failure, liquidity, and household recovery

arrows.to: trust, continued use, switching, complaint, or exit
arrows.evidence: CFPB reports institutional remediation but no customer-level trust, switching, complaint, continued use, or exit outcome
arrows.counterexample: Continued use may reflect dependence or switching cost rather than restored trust; leaving may reflect a technical alternative rather than generalized distrust
arrows.remaining_gap: Direct customer interpretation, complaint, repeat use, switching reason, trust, and exit

arrows.evidence: The CFPB page reports that, as of September 10, Bilt had reimbursed all eligible consumers—over 2,000—for $264,792.71, and that the CFPB notified Bilt on September 21 that it considered the matter closed
arrows.counterexample: Aggregate closure does not establish payment receipt, adequacy, account correction, or absence of repeat harm for every consumer
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-customer receipt, allocation, adequacy, credit/account correction, repeat failure, and later behavior

boundary: This ledger formalizes an official CFPB account of a Bilt bank-partner transition, aggregate reimbursement completion, and collaborative regulatory closure. It does not establish the full affected-customer denominator, individual payment receipt, account correction, technical durability, financial recovery, trust, or switching.
storage_boundary: Only the official CFPB account and its aggregate/agency-reported stages are retained; customer accounts, payment records, and private remediation files are not stored.
